text: ARAB 101 Beginning Arabic I Credits: 4. 4 Lecture Hours. Overview: 4 Lecture Hours. (ARAB 1411) Beginning Arabic I. Introduction to Modern Standard Arabic in its written and spoken forms; emphasis on conversation, rudimentary vocabulary, simple grammar, and reading.

ARAB 102 Beginning Arabic II Credits: 4. 4 Lecture Hours. Overview: 4 Lecture Hours. (ARAB 1412) Beginning Arabic II. Introduction of more complex grammatical constructions; vocabulary building; emphasis on putting acquired vocabulary and grammar to conversational use. Prerequisite: ARAB 101 or equivalent. Prerequisite: ARAB 101 or equivalent.

ARAB 104 Intensive Beginning Arabic Credits: 8. 8 Lecture Hours. Overview: 8 Lecture Hours. Accelerated elementary language study, with oral, listening, reading and writing practice. Equivalent to ARAB 101 and ARAB 102 .

ARAB 201 Intermediate Arabic I Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. (ARAB 2311) Intermediate Arabic I. Practice of listening, speaking and writing skills; vocabulary building; discussion of topics related to daily life and general aspects of Arab culture. Prerequisite: ARAB 102 or ARAB 104 , or equivalent. Prerequisite: ARAB 102 or ARAB 104 , or equivalent.

ARAB 202 Intermediate Arabic II Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. (ARAB 2312) Intermediate Arabic II. Emphasis on comprehending printed material, perfecting pronunciation, and attending to more complex grammar; discussion of topics holding general and professional interest; knowledge of Arab culture and history. Prerequisite: ARAB 201 or equivalent. Prerequisite: ARAB 201 or equivalent.

ARAB 204 Intensive Intermediate Arabic Credits: 6. 6 Lecture Hours. Overview: 6 Lecture Hours. Accelerated intermediate language study, with oral, listening, reading and writing practice. Equivalent to ARAB 201 and ARAB 202 . Prerequisite: ARAB 102 or ARAB 104 . Prerequisite: ARAB 102 or ARAB 104.

ARAB 215 Introduction to Modern Arab Culture Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. Exploration of cultural, linguistic, religious, and ethnic diversity in the Arab world; investigation of the impact of tradition and modernity on modern Arab culture; relating diverse cultural practices and products to diverse perspectives in the Arab world; taught in English.

ARAB 221 Introduction to Arabic Language and Society Credits: 3. 3 Lecture Hours. Overview: 3 Lecture Hours. Examination of critical linguistic issues in the Arab world from a sociolinguistic perspective, including language and religion; language and power; language and nationalism; and language and education. Prerequisite: Approval of instructor. Prerequisite: Approval of instructor.
